svg.title: Project planning and Greenfield requirements before baseline implementation
svg.desc: A single illustrative infographic combining the project-wide pre-code workflow with Greenfield URL-shortener scope, assumptions, acceptance evidence, and unverified performance targets. It distinguishes later Brownfield and Ambiguous extensions.

g.text: AI-ASSISTED ENGINEERING · PROJECT PLANNING
What happened before baseline code started?
Project-wide requirements, design, risk, acceptance, and planning — not only the Greenfield requirement.
BASELINE STAGE
Requirements and design reviewed; implementation had not yet begun.
Planning record · Oct 8–9, 2026
PRE-CODE WORKFLOW
Understand the assignment and business need
Identify the interview goal, required URL-shortener use case, intended reviewer, and prototype boundary.
Analyze and organize requirements
Separate business outcomes from service requirements, assumptions, open questions, and design inputs.
Cover scenario types and clarify meaning
Plan Greenfield, Brownfield, and Ambiguous examples; expose decisions rather than silently guessing.
Compare architecture options and risks
Record trade-offs, security/privacy risks, data flow, and technology choices as engineering decisions.
Define acceptance checks and validation evidence
Plan API, persistence, redirect, analytics, error, test, and performance verification before implementation.
Break work into tasks; review and accept the baseline
Map dependencies and AI-assistance points; candidate review/acceptance is simulated, not external sign-off.
GREENFIELD URL-SHORTENER BASELINE
Core scope and acceptance evidence
• Create a short link through a documented API.
• Persist the mapping and redirect to its destination.
• Record and retrieve click analytics.
• Verify invalid input, unknown codes, and dependency errors.
• Run tests and document the commands and results.
Assumptions and boundaries
• Accept valid absolute HTTP(S) destination URLs.
• PostgreSQL/Redis are design choices, not assignment mandates.
• Candidate review is required; no external approval is claimed.
• Human acceptance does not imply production readiness.
• Detailed privacy and alias extensions are separate scenarios.
TIMELINE CLARIFICATION
Brownfield aliases and Ambiguous tracking/security were accepted later as separate extensions, after baseline
implementation began. They are not represented as steps completed before the first code.
Architecture-supplied design targets only; not measured or claimed as met.
Illustrative reconstruction from this workspace's documentation — not a captured/verbatim AI chat or proof of historical state.
